question: Which of the following is the best description of RHUMI-1, which was seen in the news in August 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**India’s first reusable hybrid rocket**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RHUMI-1** is **India’s first reusable hybrid rocket**, which represents a major advancement in the nation's private space exploration capabilities.
 
• It was successfully launched on **August 24, 2024**, using a **mobile launcher** positioned at **Thiruvidanthai**, located on the East Coast Road in **Chennai**.
 
• The rocket was developed by **Space Zone India**, a **Chennai**-based space technology startup, in collaboration with the **Martin Group**.
 
• The mission, designated as **Mission RHUMI 2024**, reached a suborbital altitude to deploy its payloads and then successfully initiated its recovery sequence.
 
• It carried a diverse payload consisting of **3 CubeSats** and **50 PICO satellites**, which were designed to study **atmospheric conditions** and **cosmic radiation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hybrid Propulsion System**: **RHUMI-1** utilizes a **hybrid motor** that combines **solid fuel** with a **liquid oxidizer**. This technology is preferred for its **safety** and **cost-effectiveness**, as it is less prone to explosions compared to traditional solid or liquid-only engines and allows for thrust **throttling**.
 
• **Sustainability and Reusability**: The rocket features a **reusable** airframe and an **electrically triggered parachute system** for recovery. This minimizes space debris and significantly reduces the **operational costs** of deploying small satellites into orbit.
 
• **Educational Initiative**: The launch was a centerpiece of the **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Students Space Launch-2024**. This program involved thousands of students from across **India**, providing them with hands-on experience in **satellite fabrication** and **rocket science**.
 
• **Mobile Launch Capability**: Unlike traditional rockets that require fixed launch pads like those at **Sriharikota**, **RHUMI-1** was launched from a **mobile platform**. This demonstrates **flexibility** and the ability to conduct launches from diverse geographical locations with minimal infrastructure.
 
• **NewSpace India**: The success of **RHUMI-1** underscores the growing role of the **private sector** in **India's space ecosystem**, following the government's **2020 space sector reforms** that opened up the industry to non-government entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Payload Specifications**: The **50 PICO satellites** deployed are ultra-small satellites, often weighing between **0.1 kg and 1 kg**. These were programmed to monitor **environmental factors** like **accelerometer** data, **altitude**, and **UV radiation**.
 
• **Leadership**: The development was led by **Anand Megalingam**, the founder of **Space Zone India**, who aimed to make **space technology** more accessible and affordable for research and academic purposes.
 
• **Environmental Impact**: Because the hybrid motor uses non-toxic components and is **reusable**, it is considered much more **eco-friendly** than conventional expendable rockets that leave debris and chemical residues.
